solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Not so fast to admit one's saucy

indicators.note: to admit means the slow speed takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: 1 mph, one mile per hour, is a very slow speed, written here as I MPH
one's is short for 'one is', which becomes I'S

explanation.surface: Someone told to slow down replies cheekily, as if confessing to being cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so fast' looks like a command to wait, but it stands for 1 MPH, with the figure 1 read as the letter I. 'to admit' puts I'S (one's = one is) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a saucy remark or child is mischievous and cheeky, like a little imp.

clue.text: Lifeless in exposition on outskirts of Venice

parts.note: the first act of a play, Act I, is where the exposition sets out the story

indicators.note: outskirts of means only the outer letters of Venice are taken

explanation.surface: A dull exhibition on the edge of Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposition' looks like an exhibition, but it is the opening part of a play, ACT I.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something lifeless shows no movement or activity at all.

clue.text: Vegetable jelly's sickly

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
KY Jelly is a brand of lubricating gel

explanation.surface: A wobbly vegetable jelly looks unappetising.
explanation.definitionFit: PEAKY is British slang for pale and unwell, so it means sickly.

clue.text: Junction on French island gets length of tar

parts.note: a seam is the line where two pieces join
île is French for island

explanation.surface: A road junction on a French island gets a stretch of tarmac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tar' looks like road surfacing, but it is old slang for a sailor, so a 'length of tar' is a nautical measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea mile is a nautical mile, the unit of distance sailors use.

clue.text: Degenerate in pub arrested in a city long ago

indicators.note: arrested in means held inside, so the pub abbreviation sits within the other letters

parts.note: Troy was an ancient city, the setting of Homer's Iliad
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: A drinker held in custody in some ancient city goes downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to degenerate is to waste away or decline, as an unused muscle does.

clue.text: Weapon regularly upheld, carried by beastly Spanish fighter

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so the picked letters sit within the bull

parts.note: toro is Spanish for bull, the beast in a bullfight

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of upheld is taken

explanation.surface: A Spanish bullfighter is held aloft carrying a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly Spanish fighter' looks like a matador, but it is the bull itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater missile, a weapon fired from submarines and ships.

clue.text: One arranging passage of émigrés in a group going west

indicators.note: going west says the hidden letters are read backwards
passage of means the letters pass through the words émigrés in a group, which contain them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone arranges the westward journey of a party of emigrants.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft defined the answer as 'One arranging passage', but 'passage of' is the signal that the letters run through 'émigrés in a group'; 'One arranging' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who arranges things, such as events or plans, is the one who organises them.

clue.text: Like particular flush shipmate?

definitions.meaning: read playfully, made of hearts, like a poker flush in the heart suit
'me hearties' is a pirate's way of calling his fellow sailors

explanation.surface: A sailor with a ruddy, flushed complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand of all hearts is jokingly heart-like, and the word is also a sailor's term for a fellow crewman.

clue.text: Eminent Indian rejected a beer and a piece of pork

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the whole run of letters is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer
ham is a cut of meat from a pig's leg

explanation.surface: A distinguished Indian guest turns down a pint and a slice of pork, as religion or taste might dictate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the whole string A JAR A HAM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharaja was a great prince who ruled an Indian state, so he is an eminent Indian.

clue.text: Growing pain has little person in a state

indicators.note: in means the common person is placed within the other letters

parts.note: a plight is a bad state to be in
a pleb is an ordinary person, one of the little people

explanation.surface: A child with growing pains is in a real state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing pain' suggests a teenager's aches; here it is a pain to growers, a disease of orchards.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple blight is a disease of apple trees, a real pain for fruit growers.

clue.text: Mob renegade hides good silver

indicators.note: hides means the traitor keeps the other letter concealed within it

parts.note: a rat is someone who deserts their side, a renegade
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A turncoat in a gang keeps the good silverware out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragtag, as in 'ragtag and bobtail', is a disorderly rabble, a mob of common people.

clue.text: Supporter's awfully gutted after post denies Pompey's pair up front

indicators.note: after means the trimmed awfully comes behind what is left of post
denies means the word post is refused those two letters and loses them
up front says the two letters come from the start of Pompey and leave the start of post

parts.note: the first pair of letters in Pompey are P and O

indicators.note: gutted means the word awfully has its insides removed, leaving only its ends

explanation.surface: A football fan is miserable after Portsmouth's two leading players are kept off the scoresheet.
explanation.walkthrough: Pompey is the nickname of Portsmouth and its football club, which makes 'gutted' and 'post' look like football talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a prop or rope that supports something, such as a ship's mast, so it is a supporter.

clue.text: Infuse pint with meagre liquid

indicators.note: liquid means flowing and unfixed, so the letters of pint and meagre run together in a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: add a stingy measure of liquid to a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to infuse something is to fill or saturate it thoroughly, as when soaking it.

clue.text: Demanding to guard border is extremely charitable

indicators.note: to guard means to enclose protectively, so the border sits inside the other word

parts.note: an onerous task is a demanding one
a verge is a grassy border beside a road

explanation.surface: A tough job protecting a frontier is said to be very generous of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being too generous is giving beyond reason, which is charity taken to an extreme.

clue.text: Transform ground of a shrine

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters of of a shrine are reworked

explanation.surface: Change the grounds of a holy place.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to refashion something is to remake it in a new form, transforming it.

clue.text: Adventurous girl gets tan developed in European resort

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the girl's name

parts.note: Alice is the girl of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland

indicators.note: developed means changed and worked up into a new form, so the letters of tan are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl on an adventure gets a suntan on holiday at a European resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicante is a Spanish city and resort on the Costa Blanca.

clue.text: Collectively, those sharing blood group O

parts.note: a family is a group of related things, such as a family of languages
the letter O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A medical note about everyone who shares blood group O.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blood group O' reads as one phrase, but 'blood' belongs to the definition and 'group O' is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A family circle is a person's relatives taken together, the people related by blood.

clue.text: Water tick, one climbing fishing tackle

parts.note: a tick and a mo are both a moment, as in 'just a tick'
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: nets are fishing tackle

explanation.surface: A tick, a blood-sucking insect, is carried up some fishing gear out of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to water something is to wet or dampen it.

clue.text: 7 carat gold disc

parts.note: C is an abbreviation for carat
or is gold in heraldry
a dial is a round face, a disc

explanation.surface: A shopping-list description of a golden disc of so many carats.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' points to the answer at 7 down, which serves as this clue's definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer at 7 down means warm and friendly in manner, and so does this word for a warm welcome.

clue.text: Generator in Khartoum exploded, thousands evacuated

indicators.note: exploded means blown apart, so the remaining letters are scattered into a new order
evacuated means those letters are cleared out of Khartoum

parts.note: K and M are both abbreviations for a thousand

explanation.surface: A power generator blew up in Khartoum and thousands were evacuated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuated' clears K and M out of KHARTOUM, leaving HARTOU for 'exploded' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an originator or creator of something, as in the author of a plan, generates it.

clue.text: Fighter nursing leg wound

indicators.note: wound is read as the past tense of wind, so the letters of nursing and leg are twisted round

explanation.surface: A soldier is looking after an injury to their leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury noun, but it is the past tense of wind (rhymes with 'round').
explanation.definitionFit: A gunslinger is a gunfighter of the Wild West, so a fighter with a pistol.

clue.text: Position for diving fast, shunned by beginner

indicators.note: shunned by beginner means the word for fast loses its opening letter

parts.note: fast means firmly fixed, as stuck is

explanation.surface: A diving position the novice avoids because it's too quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the tuck is a diving position with knees drawn up to the chest.

clue.text: Nominal amount should cover all right

indicators.note: should cover means the number ought to enclose the approval word

parts.note: ten is an amount, a number
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A small sum ought to be enough to make everything fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as adjectives: a token payment is one in name only, merely nominal.

clue.text: Economy drive provided for us

indicators.note: for means one thing stands in place of another, here swapping in the condition word

parts.note: thrust is driving force, so drive
provided, as in 'provided that', means if

explanation.surface: A government campaign to save money has been laid on for the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' places IF in the spot where 'us' was in THRUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift is careful use of money, the same sense as economy in 'make economies'.

clue.text: Take slim man on board

parts.note: thin and slim are synonyms
the king is a chess piece, a man on the board

explanation.surface: An instruction to take a skinny person onto a ship's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' looks like a verb but is the noun, as in 'what's your take?'. 'on board' looks like a ship, but it means the chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as nouns: someone's take on a matter is their opinion or view of it.

clue.text: Items to decrease in goodness, originally robust beforehand

indicators.note: beforehand means the robust metal comes ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: iron is used for anything robust and strong, as in an iron constitution

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of goodness is used

explanation.surface: A sermon about things that reduce your virtue, with strength first in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decrease' looks like 'reduce', but read it as de-crease: ironing is the pile of clothes waiting to have their creases removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: ironing is the clothing still waiting to be pressed flat, items whose wrinkles must go.

clue.text: Flash new sugared drinks

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so the sugared word swallows the single letter

parts.note: glacé fruit is preserved in sugar, so glacé means sugared

explanation.surface: A fresh round of sweetened cocktails is served in an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a glance is a brief look, over in a flash.
